title: Characters in a Nunnery
heading: Characters in a Nunnery
requires: Playing a nun or other woman of a nunnery
summary: Advice on building nun characters: which Flaws, Virtues and Abilities fit, plus background types (the Scholar, the Refugee, the Prisoner, the Revolutionary) and which Virtues and Flaws explain why a woman ends up in a nunnery.
quotes: Most nuns come from a noble family, so Privileged Upbringing is a common Virtue.
Artes Liberales, Latin, and Church Lore are the Abilities expected of all nun characters, even if only at a low level
related: Chapter 4: The Rule and Religious Life

title: The Anchoress' Rule (Ancrene Riwle)
heading: The Anchoress' Rule (Ancrene Riwle)
requires: Playing an anchoress or her servant
summary: The rule governing an anchoress and her servants, covering speech, food, fasting, visitors, possessions and dress, which a player can adopt in part to make a character distinctively religious. Ends with ways a magical anchoress might slip out of her cell.
quotes: The primary requirements of obedience, chastity, and permanence of abode remain.

title: Mystics (female religious)
heading: Mystics
requires: Visions Flaw, or True Faith with the Understanding power
summary: Explains how to represent a religious mystic in game terms: usually the Visions Flaw, or occasionally True Faith with Understanding and Meditation. Also covers how a bishop's (or pope's) acceptance of a nun's visions earns her a Reputation as a mystic.
quotes: In most case, the experiences of a religious mystic are covered by the Visions Flaw.
related: Chapter 2: Congregation, Christian Mysticism
Realms of Power: The Divine pp.34, 36, 37, 54

title: False Visions
heading: False Visions
summary: Guidance for storyguides on non-divine sources of apparent visions (Spirits of Deceit, deluded or feigning individuals, Magic auras, faeries) and on the difficulty of proving a vision genuine, including a magus investigating inside a Dominion aura.
quotes: It can be very difficult to prove whether or not a particular mystical experience is genuinely divine.
related: Realms of Power: The Infernal p.38

title: Priests' Wives and Mistresses
heading: Priests' Wives and Mistresses
requires: Playing a priest's wife or companion
summary: Character-option advice for a woman living with a priest: the troupe decides whether the union counts as a valid marriage and whether it is a Dark Secret, and suggests roles in the parish such as a sacristan's wife.
quotes: Troupes with a female player character who lives with a priest should decide whether the priest and his wife consider themselves to be living under valid vows of marriage, or whether they believe themselves to be in a sinful relationship.
related: Realms of Power: The Divine pp.81-82

title: Heresy and Corruption
heading: Heresy and Corruption
summary: Guidance for storyguides on when heresy actually counts as Infernal rather than merely mistaken: most heretics are sincere believers, and a false teaching is Infernal only when it leads to real sinful acts.
quotes: A wrong teaching only becomes Infernal when it leads people directly to sinful behavior, and hence to damnation.
related: Realms of Power: The Dominion
Realms of Power: The Infernal

title: Cluniac Influence on Petitioning the Church
heading: Ecclesiastical Influence
requires: Favor of a Cluniac prior or abbot
summary: Cluniac abbots and priors carry extra weight with the Church hierarchy, giving a bonus to Petitioning the Church totals when their favor is won.
quotes: Gaining the favor of a Cluniac prior or abbot gives a +1 bonus to totals for Petitioning the Church (see Chapter 3: The Diocese) over and above the usual bonuses.
related: Chapter 3: The Diocese, Petitioning the Church

title: Mortuary Masses
heading: Mortuary Masses
requires: Corrupt priest
summary: Describes the Infernal perversion of a funeral Mass said for a living person, which is held to cause death and is treated as murder.
quotes: It is widely believed that if a funeral Mass is celebrated for a man or woman still living, he will die.

title: The Feast of All Souls and the Dominion
heading: The Hermit and the Devils
summary: Origin of the Feast of All Souls on 2 November, with its aura effect: on that day the Dominion is weaker than usual, Infernal auras are stronger, and some of the dead walk again.
quotes: Infernal auras increase in strength by one, and some of the dead walk once more.

title: The Corrupt Cluniacs
heading: The Corrupt Cluniacs
requires: Saga option: the Cluniacs are Infernally corrupt
summary: How to run the Cluniac order as the corrupt order in a saga: its history of corruption, the Goetic Favored Abilities and Supernatural Ability Corruption of its monks, profaned rites that create Infernal vis, Debauched Auras, and bound ghosts.
quotes: The corrupt Cluniacs have Favored Abilities of the Goetic Arts of Ablating, Binding, Commanding, and Summoning.
related: Realms of Power: The Infernal pp.14, 91, 96, 114-120
Rival Magic pp.47-74

title: Cistercian Influence on Petitioning the Church
heading: Ecclesiastical Influence
requires: Favor of a Cistercian abbot
summary: The Cistercians' standing with the papacy gives a bonus to Petitioning the Church totals when a Cistercian abbot's favor is gained.
quotes: gaining the favor of a Cistercian abbot gives a +3 bonus to totals for Petitioning the Church (See Chapter 3: The Diocese) over and above the usual bonuses.
related: Chapter 3: The Diocese, Petitioning the Church

title: Vallumbrosan Papal Influence
heading: Papal Influence
requires: Support of a Vallumbrosan abbot; petition addressed to the papacy or curia
summary: Vallumbrosan influence over the papacy adds a large bonus to the total of a petition made to the pope or curia, on top of the normal bonus for an abbot's support.
quotes: If the papacy or curia are the recipients of a petition, add +5 to the total in addition to the normal bonus for the support of an abbot.
related: Chapter 3: The Diocese, Petitioning the Church

title: The Corrupt Cistercians (Joachimite Illuminati)
heading: The Corrupt Cistercians
requires: Saga option: the Cistercians are Infernally corrupt
summary: How to run the Cistercian order as the corrupt order: the Joachimite heresy and the secret Illuminati society inside the order, with its three informal degrees of initiation culminating in an inner circle that teaches Maleficia through an Unholy Tradition.
quotes: There are three degrees of initiation into the group, though these are not formal ranks as in a mystery cult.
related: Realms of Power: The Infernal p.133
Realms of Power: The Infernal p.128

title: If the Vallumbrosans are Corrupt
heading: If the Vallumbrosans are Corrupt
requires: Saga option: the Vallumbrosans are Infernally corrupt
summary: How to run the Vallumbrosans as a diabolist order: monks are worn down until they can be offered a pact, bargaining for Virtues or loss of Flaws, with a limited term to recruit a successor before the soul is claimed.
quotes: If they leave, they have seven years to find someone else to sign the pact, or they die, their soul claimed by hell.
related: Realms of Power: The Infernal p.94

title: Templar Papal Privileges
heading: Papal Privileges
requires: Member of the Knights Templar
summary: List of the legal and religious privileges granted to the Templars by papal bulls, such as keeping booty, freedom from tithes and oaths to outsiders, and their own clergy; useful for adjudicating how Templars interact with Church and lay authority.
quotes: The order may keep the booty it captures from Muslims.
They need not pay tithes on the produce of their own lands.

title: Running a Templar Chapter Meeting
heading: Running a Chapter Meeting
requires: Templar characters
summary: Storyguide options for staging a Templar chapter meeting (mundane, mystic or dark), with a pointer to the covenant rules for designing a priory or chapterhouse.
quotes: There are broadly three options, and elements from each can be combined.
related: Covenants (church-building guidelines)
Chapter 3: The Diocese

title: The Templar Grand Master
heading: The Grand Master
requires: Knights Templar
summary: Powers and duties of the Templar grand master, including his spiritual authority over the order equal to that of a priest.
quotes: He may exercise Holy Influence over the order as if he were a priest.

title: The Grand Master's Commanding Aura
heading: The Grand Master's Commanding Aura
requires: Holding the office of Templar grand master
summary: The office of Templar grand master bestows the Commanding Aura Virtue on its holder, treated as spiritually equal to an archbishop.
quotes: The grand master, as a position appointed by God, is the spiritual equivalent to an Archbishop, with a Magic Resistance of 10.
related: Chapter 3: The Diocese

title: The Grand Master's Seal
heading: The Grand Master's Seal
requires: Holding the office of Templar grand master
summary: The grand master's seal is a Divine relic with its own Faith Score and Divine Might, which also adds extra Magic Resistance against effects tied to one particular sin.
quotes: The seal has a Faith Score of 1, granting it a Divine Might of 10.

title: Templar Brother-Knights
heading: Brother-Knights
requires: Joining the Knights Templar as a brother-knight
summary: Entry requirements, expected prior combat experience, group training and restrictions on possessions for Templar brother-knights, who are the core rank of the order.
quotes: By 1220, the Templars require a brother-knight to be of noble birth, the son of a secular knight, or the son of the daughter of a knight to be admitted to this rank.
related: Trained Group Combat

title: Templar Brother-Sergeants
heading: Brother-Sergeants
requires: Joining the Knights Templar as a brother-sergeant
summary: The commoner rank of the Templars, serving as foot soldiers and as administrators, artisans and craftsmen under the same rule as the brother-knights.
quotes: Brother-sergeants are from common backgrounds and social statuses, and are recruited from a wider area.

title: Templar Brother-Priests
heading: Brother-Priests
requires: Joining the Knights Templar as a brother-priest
summary: How priests join the Templars and the sacramental authority they hold within the order, which exceeds that of local clergy.
quotes: They can give services, celebrate Mass, hear confessions, give absolution for most offenses (except grievous sins such as murder, simony, or heresy) and bury the dead.

title: Templar Confreres and Consoeurs
heading: Confreres and Consoeurs
requires: Associate membership in the Knights Templar
summary: Lay associate members of the Templars, who take vows without full profession and may keep their own homes, including temporary-vow pilgrims and wives of Templars.
quotes: Confreres and consoeurs cannot vote in chapter meetings but otherwise interact daily with full members

title: Templar Chaplains and Petitioning
heading: Templar Chaplains and Petitioning
requires: Templar brother-priest
summary: Templar clergy petition their own commanders, the grand master or the pope rather than bishops, and may act on their own authority up to a set Ease Factor for matters within the order.
quotes: Brother-priests may, without reference to any outside authority, perform any action with an Ease Factor of 18 or less
related: Chapter 3: The Diocese, Petitioning the Church

title: Trained Group Combat (Templars)
heading: Trained Group Combat
requires: Templar brother-knights and brother-sergeants
summary: Templars who train together for a season count as a trained group in combat; without that season together they cannot form one.
quotes: who train together for a season are considered a trained group for the purpose of combat
related: ArM5 p.173

title: Templars Calling on God's Aid
heading: Calling on God's Aid
requires: Templar brother-priest or ranking Templar
summary: Templars routinely petition God's aid before battle, led by a brother-priest or, lacking one, the commanding Templar, using the Divine rules for calling on God's aid.
quotes: The Templar commander (or ranking Templar) may also call on God's aid if there is no brother-priest.
related: Realms of Power: The Divine pp.41-42

title: Templar Military Tactics
heading: Military Tactics
requires: Knights Templar
summary: How Templars fight: the cavalry charge as the centerpiece, mercenary foot and archers, siege warfare, and the black and white banner that forbids retreat while raised and serves as the rallying point.
quotes: While the banner is raised, no Templar is permitted to retreat.

title: Joining the Templars: The Membership Ritual
heading: The Membership Ritual
requires: Joining the Knights Templar
summary: Step-by-step account of the traditional ceremony in which an applicant is questioned, tested with a menial task if a commoner, swears his vows and is invested with the mantle.
quotes: Then he then swears the vows of obedience, chastity, and poverty, and promises to conquer and defend Jerusalem.

title: Joining the Templars as a Child
heading: Joining as a Child
requires: Joining the Knights Templar
summary: Children may enter the Templars as novices once old enough to bear arms, with each local commander judging fitness; orphans are usually directed elsewhere.
quotes: Ages of admission of children range from 11 to 14.

title: The Templar Rule and Penances
heading: The Templar Rule
requires: Member of the Knights Templar
summary: Outline of the Templar Rule and its penalties, from losing the mantle for a year and a day to expulsion, with a list of the offenses that earn them.
quotes: There are seven major sections to the rule
Major punishments include the stripping of a Templar's mantle for a year and a day

title: Playing a Templar Character
heading: Playing a Templar Character
requires: Knights Templar
summary: Three ways to make a Templar playable despite the strictness of the rule: loose discipline (with a Story Flaw if the rule is to matter), outside responsibilities, or a lone Templar at a remote outpost.
quotes: Templar characters should take an appropriate Story Flaw if they want to play through stories involving the rule and Templar restrictions.

title: Templar Banking, Letters of Credit and Insurance
heading: Templar Banking, Letters of Credit & Insurance
requires: Dealing with the Templars
summary: How the Templars handle deposits, letters of credit that can be redeemed at a distant priory, administration of pilgrims' assets, and a form of physical and spiritual insurance.
quotes: In exchange, they receive a letter from that priory stating the value of the deposit.
related: City and Guild

title: Templars and the Wealthy Virtue
heading: Templars and the Wealthy Virtue
requires: Templar character
summary: Templars may take the Wealthy Virtue or Poor Flaw, but these represent responsibilities, authority and free time within a regimented day instead of personal money.
quotes: Templar characters can take the Wealthy Major Virtue, and also the Poor Major Flaw.
